questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: Ragini plays the guitar with a melody.
Ragini plays the guitar with melodiousness.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word** 'melodiously'** is the correct adverb to **describe how Ragini plays the guitar.**
 
• Adjectives describe nouns, while adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
 
 
• Example: **"She sings beautifully." **('beautifully' is an adverb describing the verb 'sings')
 
• Using the correct form of words ensures clarity and precision in communication.
 
• Example: "He is a quick runner." ('quick' is an adjective describing the noun 'runner')
 
• "He runs** quickly.**" ('quickly' is an adverb describing the verb 'runs')​
 
 

Hence, the correct statement is **"*Ragini plays the guitar melodiously."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other options either use incorrect forms or do not make grammatical sense:
 
 
• Option 1:** "with a melody" is not how we typically describe playing an instrument.**
 
• Option 3: **"with melodiousness" is awkward and uncommon.**
 
• Option 4: **"melodious" is an adjective, not an adverb.**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECT preposition.

I am writing to invite you / to give a presentation / for our Jobs and Careers Conference / for engineering graduates.

options.text: I am writing to invite you
for our Jobs and Careers Conference

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the preposition 'for' used in 'for our Jobs and Careers Conference' is **incorrect.**
 
• The correct preposition should be 'at' or 'during'.
 
• The corrected sentence should be: *'I am writing to invite you to give a presentation at our Jobs and Careers Conference for engineering graduates.'*

Hence, the correct statement is:** *I am writing to invite you to give a presentation at our Jobs and Careers Conference for engineering graduates*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The prepositions 'at' and 'during' are commonly used to refer to events or periods of time.

 
 
• Example: *He spoke at the annual meeting.*
 
• Example: *She will be presenting during the conference.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) I am hearing / (B) that the heat wave / (C) is going to be / (D) worse this year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the first part of the given sentence, the phrase 'I am hearing' is incorrect.
 
• In English, the verb **'hear'** is **stative** and is not used in the continuous form.
 
• Instead of **'I am hearing'**, we should use **'I hear'** to indicate perception through the sense of hearing.
 
 
• **Example:** ***I hear** that the meeting is postponed*.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be 'I hear'.

 Hence, the correct statement is: ***I hear that the heat wave is going to be__ worse this year*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Stative verbs** describe a state rather than an action and are generally not used in the continuous form.

 
 
• **Example:** ***I believe** in fair play*.
 
 
 
• **Common stative verbs** include: *believe, know, understand, belong, contain, consist, love, hate*, etc.
 
 
• Example: ***I understand** your concerns*.

questions.question: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.

options.text: I hope your health is getting better by next week.
I hope your health will get better by next week.
I hope your health have been getting better by next week.
I hope your health is get better by next week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Future Tense: **The phrase** "will get better" **correctly uses **the future tense **to describe **an improvement in health that is expected to happen by next week.**
 
• **Verb Agreement:** The future tense is formed by using** "will"** before the base form of the verb, which in this case is **"get."**
 
• **Clarity of Intention:** Using **"will**" shows a clear intention or expectation of future improvement, which aligns with the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Context Appropriateness:** The context of the sentence is about something expected to happen in the future, making** "will get better"** the most appropriate choice.
 
• **Hope and Expectation:** The phrase** "I hope"** sets the expectation, and** "will get better"** fits logically as it refers to a future event that is hoped for.
 
• **Common Usage:** This construction is commonly used in English to express hope for future improvements or changes.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Uses present continuous tense **"is getting,"** which is incorrect for a future expectation.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect usage of **"have been getting,"** which is present perfect continuous tense, not appropriate for future hope.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect grammar as **"is get" **doesn't form a valid verb phrase.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence.

His flight departs __in__ 5:00 pm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the preposition 'in' is incorrect.
 
• The correct preposition to use with time expressions such as 5:00 pm is 'at'.
 
• Therefore, the correct preposition that should be used in place of 'in' is 'at'.

Hence, the correct sentence is: ***His flight departs at__ 5:00 pm*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Prepositions are important in indicating time, place, and direction. The preposition **'at'** is used for specific times of the day.

 
 
• **Example:** *The meeting starts **at** 3:00 pm*.
 
 
 
• The preposition **'in'** is used for longer periods, such as months, years, and parts of the day.
 
 
• Example: *She was born **in** July*.
 
 
 
• The preposition **'on'** is used for specific days and dates.
 
 
• Example: *The event is **on** Monday*.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank using the correct collocation.

We need to ________ a decision on the housing project tomorrow morning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Common Collocation: T**he phrase** "make a decision"** is a common collocation in English. A collocation is a pair or group of words that are often used together.
 
• **Standard Usage:** **"Make a decision" **is widely recognized as the standard phrase used when describing the act of deciding something.
 
• **Clarity and Understanding: **Using **"make" **in this context ensures that the sentence is clear and easily understood by native English speakers.
 
• **Context Suitability:** The act of deciding upon a project requires a definitive action, which is best encapsulated by the verb **"make."**
 
• **Decision-Making Process:** The verb **"make" **pairs naturally with **"decision"** to describe the process of coming to a conclusion or judgment.
 
• **Formality and Appropriateness: **In both formal and informal contexts, **"make a decision" is the most appropriate and conventional choice.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "Frame"** is not commonly used with "decision"; it's more appropriate for constructing sentences or policies.
 
• **Option 3: "Build" **is used for physical construction, not for decisions.
 
• **Option 4: "Draw"** is typically used with conclusions, not decisions.
